claims.text: Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".
Released PDF is 29 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.

The released cover page carries the date 2 March 2010, an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 1 December 2009 and document number DIA-08-1003-001 - the lowest DIA document number in the released set; the author field is redacted under (b)(6).
Contents run Camouflage, Transparency, Cloaking - a survey of the physics of signature reduction rather than a threat assessment.

Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Invisibility Cloaking: Theory and Experiments", series "Acquisition Threat Support", published 2010-03-02 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2009-12-01, DIA document number DIA-08-1003-001. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.
The released DIRD bears document number DIA-08-1003-001, publication date 2 March 2010 and Intelligence Cut-Off Date 1 December 2009 - the lowest document number in the released set.

a.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: commissioned under AAWSAP; lowest DIA document number in the released set
edges.note: Tier 2, and the reason is worth stating. A full-text scan of this released DIRD on 23 August 2026 found NO occurrence of the programme name anywhere in the document - unlike 27 of the 32 scanned, whose inside cover names the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program explicitly. The link therefore rests on the DIA's 9 January 2018 list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which enumerates it among the 38 reference products, and not on the document's own text.

edges.label: subject domain: transformation optics, metamaterials and signature reduction
edges.note: Contents run Camouflage, Transparency, Cloaking. The paper is the signature-reduction leg of the survey, sitting alongside Shvets's 'Metamaterials for Aerospace Applications' and against Culbreth's hypersonic detection paper. Puthoff listed signature reduction among the twelve threat areas DIA specified in the Broad Area Announcement.

edges.label: authored by Ulf Leonhardt, University of St Andrews
edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Invisibility Cloaking, Dr Ulf Leonhardt, Univ of St Andrews.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Leonhardt had been publishing on transformation optics and cloaking since 2006 and was, by the ICOD of 1 December 2009, one of the small number of internationally recognised authorities in the field. George Knapp released a copy of the DIRD in February 2019.

edges.label: series member
edges.note: Membership of the DIRD series is established by the released document itself: its cover page carries the Defense Intelligence Reference Document mark and the DIA Defense Futures banner. Publication date 2 March 2010 on the cover. 30 pages in the released copy. The cover of the scanned release is degraded, so a document number or date is asserted here only where it reads unambiguously.
